speaker: Doctor
text: Can you describe when these episodes typically occur and if you have noticed any specific triggers?

speaker: Patient
text: 59-year-old female. The patient reports a 1-month history of episodic cough and shortness of breath. The cough is nonproductive and worsens when climbing stairs and at night. She experienced fever, sore throat, and nasal congestion 8 weeks ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that history. Have you noticed any wheezing in your chest during these episodes, or any history of allergies or asthma?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Episodic cough and shortness of breath. I also have Cough worsens with exertion and at night, History of recent upper respiratory tract infection symptoms such as fever, sore throat, and nasal congestion.

speaker: Doctor
text:
REQUEST TEST: Chest_X-Ray, Spirometry. REQUEST IMAGES: Please return the Chest_X-Ray and Spirometry results.

Do you have any known allergies, family history of asthma, or do you smoke?

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Chest_X-ray: No abnormalities; Spirometry: FEV1_FVC_Ratio: 65%, FEV1: 60%

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Post-infectious Bronchospasm (or Post-infectious Asthma).

Given the normal chest X-ray, significant airflow obstruction (FEV1/FVC 65%), and symptoms worsening at night and with exertion following a recent URI, this strongly suggests airway hyperreactivity. Do you have a history of eczema or seasonal allergies, and were you ever diagnosed with asthma before this illness?
